title: Al-Qari'ah: the striking
hookLine: the Day people are like scattered moths and mountains like wool (Surah 101)

cards: On a summer night, turn on the porch light and watch. Moths come from nowhere, dozens of them, flying in every direction, bumping into the glass, into each other, into you. No order, no plan.
Just scattered. Then the mountains, solid rock for as long as anyone remembers, gone as loose as a handful of wool pulled apart.
Those are the two pictures today's surah uses for a single moment, the Day everything is shaken loose. And then it asks one simple question.

teach.h: AL-QARI'AH — THE KNOCK YOU CAN'T IGNORE.
teach.b: Surah one hundred one opens with a single word, repeated like a knock on the door. In Pickthall's translation: The Calamity! What is the Calamity?
Ah, what will convey unto thee what the Calamity is!
A day wherein mankind will be as thickly-scattered moths And the mountains will become as carded wool. Al-qari'ah comes from a root meaning to strike, to knock hard.
It's one of the Qur'an's names for the Day of Judgment: the knock you can't ignore. Notice the method. It asks: what is it?
Then: what will tell you what it is? It admits the thing is beyond words, and gives you pictures instead. Then the question.

On that Day, the surah says, whoever's scales are heavy will be in a life of contentment, and whoever's scales are light will have a pit for a home. Not how well-known you were, not how much you had. Light or heavy.
In Sunni creed the scales are real, weighing a person's deeds.
And a hadith in Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud says what weighs most: nothing is heavier on the scale than good character.
Not dramatic acts. Patience in traffic, honesty in a small deal, kindness to someone who can't repay it. The surah is short and loud, because it's meant to wake you.
What it wakes you to is quiet: the weight of ordinary deeds, adding up, every day.

how: Muslims recite al-Qari'ah in the prayers; belief in the weighing of deeds on the Day of Judgment is part of Islamic creed, and good character is often taught as the heaviest deed.

o: the drumbeat that opens a wedding feast
the Day of Judgment, which strikes like a knock
the trumpet blast that wakes the dead

games.q: what's inside the surah — tap the pairs.

s: the surah describes the Day in exact detail
it asks what will tell you what it is, and gives pictures instead.
a hadith says good character is heaviest on the scale
al-qari'ah comes from a root meaning to strike

games.q: on the Day of the striking, the surah names one thing that decides where a person ends up. what is it?
o: whether their scales are heavy or light
games.why: heavy scales, a life of contentment; light scales, the pit (101:6–9). the weight is in deeds.

practice: Pick one thing you did yesterday: the way you spoke to someone, how you handled a task, a choice about money or time.
Hold it like something in your hand and weigh it honestly, without judgment: heavy, full of care, or light, done carelessly? Then picture what would have made it heavier.

wordCard.voice: Al-Qari'ah. The striking, the knock: a name for the Day of Judgment, and the name of Surah one hundred one. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the striking, the calamity that knocks; a name for the Day of Judgment.

carryVoice: Your line: light or heavy. Nothing weighs more on the scale than good character. Day one hundred seventy-four, done.

sources.q: The Calamity! What is the Calamity? Ah, what will convey unto thee what the Calamity is! A day wherein mankind will be as thickly-scattered moths And the mountains will become as carded wool.

sources.ref: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2002; Sunan Abi Dawud 4799 (nothing heavier than good character)
